correctness.rationale: Every minimal signed root is an actual facet. Its normalized clearance is exactly a paired arc-difference constraint of weight 1 for unit roots or sqrt(2) for two-coordinate roots. Signed positive and negative maxima are exactly the nonzero literal sinks, and their antipodes are sources, so every source-to-sink path gives the sharp upper inequality rW<=2-2r. The generating arcs lie in the Fischer poset and are acyclic. Longest-source-path potentials satisfy all relaxed inequalities at r=2/(2+H); the antipodal transform is also feasible, and averaging enforces z_{-v}=-z_v and z_0=0 without losing feasibility. This proves the lower bound and the canonical center. The complete center set and longest-path tangencies follow directly from equality of normalized facet slacks.

value.rationale: Signed order polytopes are a recently introduced type-B analogue of a central family in geometric combinatorics. The theorem solves the Euclidean inball problem for every member, not a low-dimensional or symmetric slice, and reduces it to one longest-path computation in a canonical signed graph. The mixed weights 1 and sqrt(2), antipodal literal symmetry, explicit center formula, and forced tangent-path certificates are structural information not present in the source Ehrhart, triangulation, or Gorenstein theory. The result also gives an algorithmic linear-time-after-DAG-construction route to the radius.
